::: {.lead}
Give Longhaul a GitHub issue and walk away. It works for hours in a sandbox, picks up where it stopped after a crash, asks a person only at checkpoints, and ends with a pull request or an honest report of where it got stuck.
:::

::: {.hero-links}
[See the proof](results.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
[Architecture](architecture.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
[Source on GitHub]({{< meta source-repo >}}){.btn .btn-outline-secondary}
:::

## The problem

Agents can fix small, well-specified issues, yet people still sit and watch them. Left alone, an agent fails in five ways:

::: {.answer-grid}
::: {.answer-card}
**Runs die**

Every model turn and tool call is a separate step in Temporal, a workflow engine that replays work after a crash, so a crash costs one step, not the task.
:::

::: {.answer-card}
**Context fills up**

Old tool outputs shrink to stubs and old turns to progress notes, so a hundred turns fit the window.
:::

::: {.answer-card}
**Nobody knows it is stuck**

A stuck detector pauses the run and asks a person one specific question.
:::

::: {.answer-card}
**Side effects repeat**

Every GitHub write carries an idempotency key, so a retry never posts twice.
:::

::: {.answer-card}
**Cost is a surprise**

Each task has hard limits on dollars, turns and wall time, and the cost of every model call is recorded.
:::
:::

## How it works

A poller picks up issues labeled `longhaul` and starts one Temporal workflow for each. A planner, a coder and a verifier work inside it, and every change in the workspace is a git checkpoint, so a retried tool call never runs on half-applied edits.

::: {.diagram-fit}
```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-overview
%%| column: page
%%| fig-cap: "The life of one task. The architecture page has every step."
flowchart LR
  ISSUE(["Issue labeled<br/>longhaul"]) --> PLAN["Planner reads the repo<br/>and posts a plan"]
  PLAN -->|approved, when the<br/>repo asks for it| CODE["Coder works in turns:<br/>model turn, tool call,<br/>git checkpoint"]
  CODE -->|finish| VERIFY["Verifier runs the tests<br/>and reviews the diff"]
  VERIFY -->|send back| CODE
  VERIFY -->|pass| PR(["Pull request<br/>with a run report"])
  CODE -->|stuck or<br/>out of budget| PAUSE["Pause and ask<br/>one question"]
  PAUSE -->|hint or top-up| CODE
  VERIFY -->|fails 3 times| STUCK(["Report of where<br/>it got stuck"])
  PAUSE -->|no answer in time| STUCK
```
:::

Repo code runs only in a sandbox that holds no credentials. The agent never pushes to a default branch, and a person merges every pull request. The [architecture page](architecture.qmd) shows the parts, and the [decisions page](decisions.qmd) says why each was chosen.

## The proof

The chaos suite kills the worker, the sandbox, Temporal and Postgres while recorded tasks run. Then it checks the pull request, the diff, and every write on a fake GitHub set up for that run.

::: {fragment="_generated/chaos-tiles.md"}
:::

::: {fragment="_generated/chaos-chart.md"}
:::

The model evaluation (SWE-bench Verified and a custom task set) has not run yet, so this site makes no claim about how well the agent codes. The [results page](results.qmd) has the method, the limits and the full table.

## See it

The console lists every task, shows each one turn by turn, and holds the forms to approve a plan, send a hint, add budget or cancel. The screenshots come from the demo stack, so every cost on them is $0.00.

![The tasks list: each row shows the task's phase, turns, cost and outcome, and the two tasks that wait on a person say what they need. Select it to see it whole.](_generated/docs/gates/media/phase-9/1-tasks-1280.png){.screenshot .screenshot-top}

The [console page](console.qmd) has every screen.

## Try it

You need Docker, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Python 3.12. No API key and no GitHub account: a scripted provider plays a fixed set of model answers.

```bash
git clone {{< meta source-repo >}}.git
cd longhaul-autonomous-coding-agent-github
make setup && make up && make demo
```

`make demo` runs one task on a small package whose `add()` subtracts, prints the final diff and stops. To point Longhaul at your own repo, follow [Run on your repo]({{< meta source-repo >}}#run-on-your-repo) in the README.
